correctness.rationale: The source data determine a unique systematic generator \(G=[I_{11}\mid T]\). Exact elimination gives \(\operatorname{rank}G=11\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(GG^{\mathsf T})=1\), so the standard hull formula gives dimension \(10\). A nullspace basis generates the hull and has zero Gram matrix. Complete enumeration of \(3^{11}\) ambient words, \(3^{10}\) hull words, and both nonzero hull cosets verifies every enumerator coefficient and the distances \(8\) and \(9\). The Griesmer sum for a ternary \([22,10,10]\) code is \(23\), proving that hull distance \(9\) is globally optimal among ternary linear \(\([22,10]_3\)\) codes.

value.rationale: The hull is a natural structural invariant for a rate-one-half isodual code because it measures the exact failure of self-duality and controls the intersection with the dual. Here the unique non-circulant/non-negacirculant DT-optimal class sits at the extremal boundary: its hull has the largest possible proper dimension, and that hull is itself a globally distance-optimal self-orthogonal \([22,10,9]_3\) code. The exact hull and quotient-coset spectra explain how the ambient optimal code is assembled and provide a reusable fingerprint for equivalence checks. This is more than a routine recomputation of the published minimum distance.
